goals.description: Before medication initiation, confirm elevated blood pressure on at least two separate occasions, review the current medication list and comorbidities, and review baseline BMP renal function and electrolytes.
Complete a BMP 4 weeks after medication initiation to monitor renal function and electrolytes.
Use a validated upper-arm device to obtain and submit home blood pressure readings weekly; ensure the care team reviews the weekly average.
Review the seven-day home blood pressure average 2 to 4 weeks after the medication change.
Notify the responsible clinician when the weekly home blood pressure average is at least 135/85 mmHg, or exceeds a lower clinician-set threshold if applicable.
Follow a DASH-style eating pattern and limit sodium intake to less than 2,300 mg per day.
Work toward and maintain a BMI of 18.5–24.9 kg/m2; if above the healthy range, pursue an initial 5–10% weight loss.
Limit alcohol intake to no more than 2 drinks per day for men or 1 drink per day for women; confirm which limit applies rather than inferring it when relevant information is absent.
Achieve at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity or 75 minutes per week of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity.
If the patient smokes, receive smoking-cessation counseling and resources.
Inform the patient of blood pressure status, involve the patient in shared decision-making, and provide lifestyle education materials at diagnosis.
When treatment criteria are met, ensure an EHR alert notifies the clinical team so the treatment recommendation is addressed.
If a week passes without home readings, send a reminder; after three reminders on different days without readings, contact the patient to identify barriers.

Track hypertension guideline adherence measures, including timely blood pressure documentation, appropriate treatment initiation, recommended ACE-inhibitor laboratory monitoring, and timely review of submitted home readings.

One medication initiation goal covers the applicable criteria: (After prerequisites are met, initiate lisinopril 10 mg orally daily for hypertension, given SBP 142 mmHg with diabetes and no kidney disease) OR (Complete a clinical follow-up visit 2 weeks after medication initiation to review blood pressure response and medication tolerability).

activities.description: Before medication initiation, confirm elevated blood pressure with measurements on at least two separate occasions; review the current medication list, including over-the-counter medicines; assess diabetes and kidney disease status; obtain baseline BMP; and review baseline renal function and electrolytes.
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG assessment section requires confirmation on separate occasions and baseline laboratory assessment. Baseline BMP renal function and electrolytes must be reviewed before starting medication.

activities.description: After the required blood pressure confirmation and baseline BMP review, start lisinopril 10 mg orally daily. Before initiation, assess pregnancy possibility and status when applicable; do not use lisinopril during pregnancy Initiate only after elevated blood pressure is confirmed with at least two measurements on separate occasions and a clinician has reviewed baseline BMP renal function and electrolytes.
activities.clinicalRationale: The treatment DMN selected medication initiation and lisinopril 10 mg daily for SBP 142 mmHg, diabetes, and no kidney disease. This meets the CPG criterion of SBP at least 130 mmHg with diabetes and no kidney disease; the first-line therapy recommendation specifies lisinopril 10 mg daily. Pregnancy assessment and avoidance during pregnancy are supplemental medication-safety precautions.

activities.description: Schedule and complete a clinical follow-up visit 2 weeks after medication initiation to review response and tolerability.
activities.clinicalRationale: The treatment DMN specifies a 2-week follow-up interval. This is a clinical visit to review response and tolerability, distinct from the home-average review and BMP timing.

activities.description: Order and review a basic metabolic panel to monitor renal function and electrolytes after starting medication.
activities.clinicalRationale: The monitoring DMN specifies BMP at 4 weeks when medication is started and kidney disease is absent. The CPG states that patients starting ACE-inhibitor therapy require BMP monitoring.

activities.description: Use a validated upper-arm blood pressure device. Take two readings one minute apart in the morning before medications and two readings one minute apart in the evening, on at least 3 and preferably 7 consecutive days; transmit readings to the care team weekly by patient portal, secure messaging, or telephone. The care team reviews the weekly average.
activities.frequency: Daily readings for at least 3 and preferably 7 consecutive days; submit and review weekly
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG recommends home monitoring after a treatment decision and defines the measurement schedule and weekly submission. A home average of at least 135/85 mmHg is considered equivalent to an office reading of 140/90 mmHg.

bindings.name: instructions_text
bindings.value: All patients in whom a treatment decision has been made under Table 1 should perform home blood pressure monitoring using a validated upper-arm device. Patients should take two readings one minute apart in the morning before medications and two readings one minute apart in the evening, on at least three and preferably seven consecutive days, and transmit their readings to the care team weekly through the patient portal, secure messaging, or telephone.

bindings.name: reminder_text
bindings.value: Please submit this week's home blood pressure readings.

bindings.name: escalation_reason
bindings.value: No home blood pressure readings after reminders.

bindings.name: notify_reason
bindings.value: Weekly home blood pressure average above threshold.

bindings.name: repeat_instructions_text
bindings.value: Any single reading above 180/120 mmHg should be repeated after five minutes.

bindings.name: same_day_contact_text
bindings.value: If it remains above 180/120 mmHg the patient should contact the clinic the same day.

activities.description: Review the seven-day home blood pressure average 2 to 4 weeks after the medication change, in addition to the separately scheduled clinical visit and laboratory monitoring.
activities.frequency: Once 2 to 4 weeks after the medication change
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG calls for review of the seven-day home average 2 to 4 weeks after a medication change, separately from laboratory follow-up.

activities.description: Notify the responsible clinician when the weekly home average is at least 135/85 mmHg, or above a lower threshold set by the clinician for diabetes or kidney disease. For any single reading above 180/120 mmHg, repeat after 5 minutes; if it remains above 180/120 mmHg, contact the clinic the same day. If a reading above 180/120 mmHg is accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, a vision change, or difficulty speaking, call emergency services immediately.
activities.frequency: For each weekly average and whenever a severe individual reading occurs
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG specifies routine clinician notification thresholds and same-day clinic contact for persistent readings above 180/120 mmHg. The emergency-services symptom pathway is supplemental safety guidance from the American Heart Association. Supplemental emergency-symptom guidance follows the American Heart Association: https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings/when-to-call-911-for-high-blood-pressure.

activities.description: Adopt a DASH-style eating pattern emphasizing fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy; limit saturated fat and sodium to less than 2,300 mg per day.
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG recommends DASH dietary changes and sodium restriction as lifestyle measures for blood pressure management.

activities.description: Work toward and maintain a BMI of 18.5–24.9 kg/m2; if above the healthy range, pursue a 5–10% weight reduction.
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG identifies healthy weight maintenance and modest weight loss as measures that can reduce blood pressure.

activities.description: Limit alcohol intake to no more than 2 drinks per day for men and 1 drink per day for women, as stated in the CPG; confirm which limit applies before counseling.
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG provides separate alcohol limits by sex. Both source limits are preserved, and the applicable limit is not inferred when relevant information is absent.

activities.description: Engage in at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking, or at least 75 minutes per week of vigorous-intensity aerobic exercise.
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG recommends regular aerobic activity as a lifestyle measure for blood pressure management.

activities.description: If the patient smokes, provide smoking-cessation counseling and resources.
activities.frequency: Assess smoking status and offer support as applicable
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG conditionally recommends smoking-cessation support when applicable.

activities.description: Inform the patient of blood pressure status, involve the patient in shared decision-making about treatment options, and provide lifestyle-modification education materials at diagnosis.
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG recommends communicating blood pressure status, shared decision-making, and lifestyle education at diagnosis.

activities.description: Use EHR-integrated decision support alerts to notify clinicians when blood pressure readings and documented comorbidities meet pharmacological treatment criteria.
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG conditionally recommends EHR-integrated alerts to support timely clinician action when pharmacological criteria are met.

activities.description: If a week passes without submitted home blood pressure readings, send a reminder. After three reminder attempts on different days without readings, contact the patient directly to identify monitoring barriers.
activities.frequency: Reminder after one week without readings; direct contact after three attempts on different days
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG specifies reminders for missing weekly readings and direct contact after three unsuccessful reminders to identify barriers.

activities.description: Track guideline adherence measures: blood pressure documented within the past 12 months; appropriate pharmacological therapy within 30 days when treatment criteria are met; ACE-inhibitor laboratory monitoring within the recommended timeframe; and care-team review of submitted weekly home readings within 7 days.
activities.frequency: Ongoing; assess each measure at its stated interval
activities.clinicalRationale: The CPG recommends these measures to monitor implementation and timeliness of hypertension care.

Work toward and maintain a BMI of 18.5–24.9 kg/m2; if above the healthy range, pursue an initial 5–10% weight loss.

When treatment criteria are met, ensure an EHR alert notifies the clinical team so the treatment recommendation is addressed.
